design: none
note: 4 TMs, 9 aa of extracellular face across two loops of 4 and 5 residues, both termini cytoplasmic, no signal peptide, no N-glycosylation sites. The size cap was never its problem. Drop it. Verified independently here: it is absent from the surfaceome canonical tier and present only in likely.

design: mini-PCDH15-V4: delete EC4-EC8, one synthetic EC3-EC9 junction, keep EC9-10 flexibility
risk: Two synthetic junctions is the documented failure mode - V7 was toxic in control mice, V8 dead. Do not improvise a shorter variant. Obligate parallel homodimer. Shedding untested.
note: Build on the human CD2 backbone Q96QU1-4 (1,783 aa), the isoform the published work uses, which also buys ~180 aa over the UniProt canonical. All eight published variants reached the plasma membrane in HEK293 including the non-functional V8, so surface display is de-risked but tells you nothing about the fold.

design: CR1-AD: signal peptide + LHR-A (CCP1-7) joined to LHR-D (CCP22-28) + CCP29-30 + native stalk, TM and tail
risk: Keeps the C4b site, loses both C3b sites; no design under 1,535 aa keeps all three. The YZ1 antibody epitope is absent from LHR-D, so a common anti-CR1 reagent will stain truncation-dependently. LHR repeats are over 99 percent identical, a recombination and assembly hazard.
note: Klickstein 1988 built piAD and piCD as membrane constructs, surface-labelled by iodination and immunofluorescence and surface-functional by rosetting. One LHR deleted is not enough: that is about 1,590 aa, still over. Use CR1-CD instead if the readout is complement engagement rather than display.

design: membrane-proximal FN3 block: signal peptide + FN3-27 to FN3-34 + juxtamembrane + native TM + full tail
risk: The one published membrane-displayed fragment used a heterologous PDGFR anchor and permeabilised immunofluorescence, not a true surface stain. Usherin expresses poorly in culture. Shedding untested.
note: Corrects our own note: exon-13 skipping is 214 aa, about 4 percent of the protein, and is not a size precedent at all. The real precedent is Yang lab 2020, where a membrane-proximal FN3 block was displayed at the plasma membrane while the laminin half aggregated.

design: beta4-less minireceptor: signal peptide + ECD 21-1350 + juxtamembrane stub + native TM, intracellular domain deleted
risk: ER retention is the documented failure mode, not hypothetical. Needs the MESD chaperone for surface delivery, the LRP4 analogue of LRP1 needing RAP. ADAM10 sheds the ectodomain. The beta3-to-juxtamembrane junction has never been made.
note: No published LRP4 construct is both ectodomain-shortened and surface-shown. 21-1350 is literature-exact from Xie 2023 but that construct was built to secrete. Only about 49 aa of headroom for the tag. Build with a surface-expression arm or defer.

design: GPS-cleaved C-terminal fragment: CD5 leader + T3049 to C-terminus, all 11 TMs
risk: Needs PKD2 as an ER chaperone; the published work used plain HEK293T, which carries endogenous PKD2, so PKD2-independence is not proven. WT CTF is a constitutively active tethered-agonist receptor - the stalkless variant drops that while trafficking equally well.
note: Starting at 3049 deletes the GAIN/GPS module, so there is no autoproteolysis and nothing to shed. Surface biotinylation measured directly. Keeping all 11 TMs costs only 1,229 aa, so no single-TM fallback is needed. The tag must go N-terminal or in an extracellular loop - the native C-terminus is cytoplasmic.

design: delta-EC4-27: signal peptide + EC1-EC3 (1-348) fused to 2975-3354 (EC27 membrane-proximal, TM, full tail)
risk: The EC3-EC27 junction is non-native and uncharacterised; cadherin EC-EC linkers coordinate calcium. Homophilic aggregation may cause clumping in a pooled library. GOPC/PIST traps CDH23 in the trans-Golgi, so a high-GOPC line could suppress display - the delta-ITEL variant mitigates.
note: Overturns our own note. We recorded "no working mini-CDH23 yet"; Xu 2010 built exactly this, membrane-anchored, and measured it by non-permeabilised anti-Myc staining. All four boundaries verified here against UniProt Q9H251: signal 1-23, EC3 ends 348, EC27 ends 2975, TM 3065-3085. Yoshimura 2023 was a triple-AAV delivery failure, not a verdict on truncation. Zheng 2010 gives the floor: ~26 extracellular residues fails.

design: signal peptide + Ig1-Ig6 + one membrane-proximal FN3 stalk + native TM and tail
risk: UniProt annotates NO signal peptide for SDK1 and the protein opens with a 98-residue Gly-rich extension; the mature protein starts at Q99. Verified here. Building from residue 1 would give a construct with no leader. Use a validated heterologous leader spliced onto Q99. The published surface-detection antibody binds FN3 domains the construct deletes.
note: Deleting the 13-FN3 stalk makes the molecule short and rigid, which shifts the cis/trans balance the stalk flexibility creates - a real behavioural change, not a neutral deletion.

design: signal peptide + Ig1-Ig6 + one membrane-proximal FN3 stalk + native TM and tail
risk: Same cis/trans caveat as SDK1. Signal peptide is cleanly annotated here (1-20, mature Q21), unlike SDK1.
note: Ig1-Ig4 is the crystallographic homophilic interface and Ig1-2 carries most of the affinity, so Ig1-6 is generous. Cytoplasmic tail is proven dispensable - full-length Sdk with the ICD replaced by a fluorescent protein still adheres and clusters.

design: signal peptide + Ig1-Ig9 + FN3-6 + native TM and tail
risk: No vertebrate domain mapping exists. The only human DSCAM ectodomain data is an unpublished thesis reporting Ig1-4 monomeric in solution, which points away from the fly mechanism. Keep the native cytoplasmic tail - a single tail missense abolishes DSCAML1 surface delivery.
note: Full-length human DSCAM surface-expresses, but no truncation has ever been built. Ig1-9 is kept rather than Ig1-4 because the only mechanistic data is Drosophila Dscam1, where the interface spans Ig1-8 and needs Ig7.

design: signal peptide + Ig1-Ig9 + FN3-6 + native TM and tail
risk: As DSCAM. The A2105T cytoplasmic missense is retained intracellularly and fails to aggregate, so the tail is not safely editable in this family.
note: Cheapest of the set to settle empirically rather than bibliographically - the aggregation and surface-stain assays are standard for all four.

design: none
risk: Deleting both nucleotide-binding domains and the C-terminal tail still leaves it 143 aa over budget, so any fitting design must delete a whole transmembrane half. The two extracellular domains co-fold into one tunnel, so removing ECD2 orphans ECD1. Of fourteen published HA-insertion constructs, five failed surface biotinylation outright.
note: Drop. Nothing shortened has ever been shown at the ABCA1 surface, and the only surface-specific data on engineered ABCA1 is a list of constructs that failed to traffic.

design: residues 1-577: cytoplasmic N-terminus, TM1, ECD1, TM2
leader: none needed, TM1 is a signal anchor
risk: The one construct of this shape is a disease frameshift allele, and its plasma-membrane call rests on permeabilised imaging in a paper whose own abstract lists ER first. A clean stop at 577 has never been tested. The mirror-image truncation, missing residues 1-138, is ER-retained.
note: Worth one shot only because an African-ancestry 44-bp deletion allele happens to be exactly the ECD1-anchored construct we would have designed. De-risk with non-permeabilised anti-ECD1 staining or surface biotinylation, the two assays this literature lacks.

design: MUC4/Y, a natural splice isoform lacking the tandem-repeat exon: own signal peptide 1-28 joined to 4265-5412
risk: The alpha/beta split at 4687/4688 means the NIDO/AMOP half can dissociate, leaving only MUC4-beta tethered. Tightest headroom of the four mucins at about 359 aa.
note: Replaces the mini-MUC4 our note currently cites, which is about 3,000 aa and roughly twice over budget. MUC4/Y is a natural isoform, so it needs no exogenous leader - the only mucin here that does not.

design: MUC17-3TR: exogenous leader + 3 tandem repeats + full SEA + EGF + TM + tail; or the minimal SEA+TM form
risk: Sheds on vesicles, more so under TNF-alpha. No residue number upstream of the SEA is portable between a paper and UniProt canonical, because repeat counts are allele-specific.
note: The published forward primer is ATGGAGACAGACACACTCC, which this session verified is base-for-base the first 19 nt of the Igk leader we sourced from the Thermo manual. The field already uses our exact leader for this exact problem. A minimal form replacing the whole repeat domain with a tag is also published and surface-confirmed by FACS, the direct analogue of MUC16 c114.

design: by homology: C-terminal fragment with EGF + SEA + TM + tail
risk: Only about 65 PubMed records mention MUC12 at all, and the one mechanistic paper shows SEA cleavage, not surface delivery. SEA domains are explicitly not interchangeable between MUC1, MUC3 and MUC12, so no chimeric SEA.
note: No surface-verified construct of its own. Inherits the family recipe only.

design: by homology: C-terminal fragment with EGF + SEA + TM + tail
risk: Nomenclature trap: UniProt lists MUC3 as a synonym of MUC17, and the rodent Muc3 literature may be MUC17 evidence rather than MUC3A. Check a paper's C-terminal sequence before trusting it - MUC3A ends KRPEMTSSSV, MUC17 ends IQRPQVMTTSF.
note: The only human MUC3A sequence with surface evidence is its 73-residue cytoplasmic tail carried on a MUC17 body. No human MUC3A ectodomain construct exists.

design: C-terminal pore module: cytoplasmic loop + TM37 + extracellular cap + TM38 + tail, human 2077-2521
risk: The module is constitutively open and pressure-insensitive - an always-on calcium-permeable channel will likely be counterselected in a pooled library. Use a pore-dead mutant. Obligate homotrimer, and the apical epitope loop is formed from all three subunits, so a monomer cannot display it. Both termini are cytoplasmic, so the tag must go inside the cap.
note: Overturns the premise in my own brief. PIEZO1 does have a real extracellular face - the 234-residue cap is the Er blood group antigen, and human alloantibodies bind it on intact red cells. Published boundaries are mouse; the human transposition needs alignment before ordering.

design: C-terminal pore module by analogy to PIEZO1, human 2313-2752
risk: As PIEZO1, plus no evidence any PIEZO2 pore module folds or traffics, and no antigenicity data for its cap.
note: The PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 caps are functionally interchangeable in chimeras, which is the basis for transferring the design. Nothing published fits the budget.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: Constitutively active once the autoinhibitory sema brace is deleted - expect cell rounding and selection against high expressers in a pooled library. Pair with a GAP-dead arm.
note: The only dECD plexin with a published surface measurement in its own gene, by extracellular MYC epitope, permeabilised against non-permeabilised.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: As PLXNA1.
note: Has its own construct: A2InTm, residues 1214-1894, TM plus intracellular, already in a lentiviral vector, rescuing proliferation and soft-agar colony formation in PLXNA2-knockout U87MG as well as full-length does. Note it carries no signal peptide at all and only 24 juxtamembrane residues, so its TM must act as a signal anchor - our signal peptide plus 30-residue stub is an improvement on it, not a copy.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: No delta-ECD, delta-sema or constitutively active membrane-anchored PlexinA3 exists - the genuine gap in the A-class. Whether its weak Sema3A response is a coupling problem or a delivery problem has never been tested, so this is the gene most deserving of a surface stain.
note: Downgraded. An earlier pass claimed the Sema3A deficit resolves as co-receptor pairing rather than trafficking; that was over-confident and is retracted. The later literature contradicts the blanket claim - A3 contributes to both Sema3F and Sema3A signalling in knockout mice - so the deficit is assay-specific, but the trafficking question is unresolved, not settled.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: As PLXNA1.
note: Has its own construct: delta-NT, whole ectodomain truncated, myc-tagged, collapsing most transfected COS-7 cells. Companion delta-sema and delta-Ig variants were surface-verified by anti-myc on non-permeabilised cells plus surface biotinylation.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: Class B: the C-terminus is a PDZ-binding motif ending VENKVTDL that docks PDZ-RhoGEF. Do not put a tag, barcode or readthrough cassette there - a deliberate deltaVTDL mutant exists as a known loss-of-function control.
note: Citation corrected. Our precedents doc credited a PLXNB2 delta-ECD to Pinskey 2022; that paper has none, verified here against the PMC full text. The real construct is Huang 2021, a human lentiviral dEcto deleting 30-1189, Addgene 86238 - functional, but nobody has measured surface expression of a PLXNB2 delta-ECD. That construct leaves only 18 residues of stub, so our 30 is conservative.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: The only gene in the family with no truncation precedent of any kind, now confirmed rather than merely unsearched - the published B3 deletions go the opposite way, removing the intracellular domain and keeping the ectodomain. Plus the erroneous-initiation N-terminus. Build from the full-length 1,909 aa ORF, not an EST-derived variant: B3 has 3-prime splice variants that truncate the C-terminus and lose the PDZ motif.
note: Full-length PLXNB3 surface expression is directly proven by surface biotinylation, so the gene traffics fine on its own. Two RXXR convertase sites imply a natural sema-less membrane species, but it has never been isolated and no residue numbers exist.

design: delta-ectodomain plus a 30-residue juxtamembrane stub
risk: Anoikis. The published delta-EC construct detaches MDCK cells from matrix and then kills them, and suppresses proliferation in H441 and U87-MG - so in a pooled library this arm may be actively selected against. Its rescue was co-expressed Rap1 G12V. Surface localisation was never directly measured; the evidence is functional. The paper's stated coordinates have digits dropped and are unusable, so boundaries come from UniProt. The juxtamembrane stub is itself an ADAM10 substrate, so an N-terminal tag could be shed off and read as absent expression.
note: Upgraded from needs-deeper-search: Toyofuku 2025 built a gene-specific delta-EC construct, membrane-active and constitutively active without Sema3E. Loses the MET interaction that lives in the deleted ectodomain. GAP output is Rnd2-gated, so this is inert rather than active in a Rnd2-null line.

design: P-subunit equivalent: signal peptide + Ig1-3 + the natural 85-residue juxtamembrane stub + TM + both PTP domains
risk: Shedding is the dominant risk and it lands inside the stub we must keep. The cut is mapped to P1275-I1276, seven residues from the TM, so after shedding about six residues of ectodomain remain and any tag placed in the stub is lost with it. Put the tag in the Ig block or on the cytoplasmic terminus. Shedding is then followed by internalisation and a gamma-secretase cut.
note: The family is naturally cleaved by furin into an E-subunit and a P-subunit that reach the surface as a complex, so the truncation we want already exists as a native species. Cutting at the furin site removes the recognition sequence, so the construct is never furin-cleaved and its mature N-terminus comes from signal peptidase instead.

design: as PTPRS
risk: As PTPRS. The shedding site is not homologous in PTPRF and has never been mapped, so it cannot be mutated out without mapping it first.
note: Corrects our own note, which reads as though the LAR P-subunit were a published standalone construct. It is not - it is the native furin product. PTPRF gives the topology from its own gene and inherits expressibility as a short ORF from PTPRS.

design: as PTPRS
risk: As PTPRS. A PTPRD construct with an intact D2 domain will trans-inhibit endogenous PTPRS in the host line - a real off-target effect, not a theoretical one.
note: A natural isoform lacking four of the eight FN3 domains exists, so the gene tolerates a large ectodomain deletion as an expressed product, but no designed deep truncation with surface staining has been published.

design: tethered-agonist CTF from the GPS site, or the published double deletion of CADH1-8 and CADH9-GAIN
risk: Constitutively active: a CTF exposes the tethered agonist, so every transduced cell carries a Gs signal. Route B deletes the agonist entirely. Neither construct adheres or localises to cell-cell junctions, since CADH1-8 carries that function.
note: Both halves of the double deletion were built separately in mouse CELSR1 and each reached the surface, measured on non-permeabilised cells by N-terminal HA staining. The published CADH9-GAIN deletion alone is about 1,658 aa in human and does not fit.

design: tethered-agonist CTF from the GPS site 2356/2357
risk: As CELSR1. A CTF presents only about 21-24 extracellular residues before TM1 plus the three loops, so it is a poor antigen if a substantial displayed ectodomain is wanted.
note: The one gene in the family whose GPS cleavage position UniProt states outright. Bui 2023 built exactly this with an exogenous PAR1 leader and surface-labelled it, and their other constructs used an IgK leader - our exact choice, precedented again.

design: tethered-agonist CTF by alignment to CELSR2
risk: Least tolerant of tinkering in the family: a point mutation inside the tethered agonist significantly reduced surface expression and was dropped from the published analysis. Keep that sequence native.
note: Cleavage-deficient like CELSR1 - the catalytic residue is a glycine - so a CELSR3 CTF does not mimic a naturally occurring species. The start residue must be re-derived from sequence at build time rather than taken on faith.

design: signal peptide + cadherin repeats 1-4 + a membrane-proximal EGF/LamG cassette + TM + full tail
risk: A furin site in the membrane-proximal LamG is a prerequisite for ADAM10 shedding, which would leave only a p60 remnant and destroy the display. Use the short cassette, which drops that LamG, or mutate the motif. Removing about 28 contiguous cadherin repeats is a bigger splice than any precedent we hold.
note: No published shortened membrane-anchored FAT construct with a surface readout exists for any FAT. The fallback with real data behind it is an ectodomain swap onto the FAT1 TM and tail.

design: as FAT1
risk: As FAT1; its furin site is unpublished and must be found by alignment.
note: Nothing gene-specific published.

design: as FAT1 but the short cassette is mandatory
risk: As FAT1. The full cassette is 1,651 aa and does not fit.
note: The FAT4-DCHS1 interface is a solved co-crystal, but of a soluble fragment, not a membrane-anchored construct. A second C-terminal binding site was reported in 2024 and this design deletes it.
